mode_evidence: The text reports the operator 'seeing' disk, stars, doors of fire, lightnings and a fiery god in the air, with the eyes open or shut at different stages. Mead's commentary reads these as projections of the operator's own soul-powers ('appearances will differ according to the mind-content'), 'visions... presented to the inner eye', so the boundary between perceptual and imaginal is left open.
onset_evidence: The rite is explicitly for those already prepared: the Father hands it to a worthy initiate son. Mead says it is 'intended only for those who have already made themselves ready'. No instruction for someone who sees nothing, apart from the breath step; the first result (feeling light, rising in the air) is predicted, not troubleshot. Transmission from Father to Son is stated as a condition.

conditions.posture: body reduced to absolute quietude before the breathing (Mead)
conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: gaze at the sun's rays; later eyes closed for one utterance and then opened; 'gaze intently' in the air at the god
conditions.prerequisites: initiation; purification; worthy to receive the craft from a Father
conditions.other: silence gesture (finger on lips), hissing and puffing sounds, a prolonged 'bellowing' with belly pressure to start the senses going

stages.label: ascent
stages.description: After three deep breaths from the sun's rays the operator seems lifted into mid-air and sees the gods ascending and descending through the sun's disk.

stages.label: disk expands
stages.description: After the second utterance, a mighty host of five-pointed stars emerges from the disk and fills the air; then doors of fire fast closed.

stages.label: the god
stages.description: A youthful god with locks of flame, white tunic, scarlet mantle and crown of fire; later lightnings leap from his eyes and stars from his body.

what_to_do_with_light: Stop hostile or blurred appearances with the Silence utterance; gaze intently at the god; salute and address him.
obstacles_and_fixes: Gods gazing sternly and bearing down: finger on lips, 'Silence', hiss and puff, and they turn benign
Operator confused by the panorama: another utterance of Silence
Senses not started: bellow with belly-pressure
cautions: Mead: the first visions are so overwhelming that the appearances are blurred and seem hostile
The rite is restricted to the prepared and initiated
interpretation: A theurgic ascent: the sun's light and breath are used to lift the operator to see the Lord of the cosmos. Mead reads the ascending and descending gods as the man's own soul-powers.
practice_summary: In sunlight, after purification and with the body still, draw breath from the sun's rays by inhaling three times as deeply as possible. The text promises a sense of rising into the air and sight of the gods moving through the sun's disk and a pipe hanging from it. If the gods seem hostile, lay a finger on the lips, say Silence, hiss and puff. Repeat with the second utterance and the disk expands, releasing five-pointed stars; doors of fire appear. Close the eyes for the long invocation, open them, and gaze intently into the air for lightnings and the god, finishing with a bellow to bring the senses into play. It is given only to a prepared initiate.

Take  from  the  [Sun-]rays  breath,
inhaling  thrice  [as  deeply]  as  thou  canst
key_passages.paraphrase: Draw breath from the sun's rays, inhaling three times as deeply as possible, and the ascent is seen.

key_passages.anchor:
and  straightway  shalt  thou  see  a  mighty

key_passages.paraphrase: After the second utterance a host of five-pointed stars comes out of the disk and fills the air.

the  Ritual  is  intended  only  for  those
who  have  already  made  themselves  ready
key_passages.paraphrase: Mead: the rite presupposes prior preparation; it is not for a beginner who sees nothing.

key_passages.anchor:
are  of  so  sublime  a  nature  that  he  cannot
hold  himself  steady,  but  is  shaken,
key_passages.paraphrase: The first visions shake the operator so that the appearances blur and seem hostile; Silence calms them.

key_passages.anchor: Air  intently,  and  thou  shalt  see  light
key_passages.paraphrase: Gazing intently in the air, the operator is to see lightning flashes, trembling lights and a descending god.

confidence_note: Digest only; a ritual script with no accounts of how the visions arise in practice.
